Package index

Analyze a test

Start here. lactate_threshold() takes the stages of a step test (intensity, lactate and, optionally, heart rate) and estimates every threshold method in one call. It returns a tibble that remembers the data and the fitted curve, so it can be plotted, checked and turned into zones afterwards.

lactate_threshold()
Lactate thresholds from a step test
demo_data
Demo data
lactate_tests
Lactate step tests from different sports, athletes and scenarios
lactate_curve()
Lactate curve

Look at the results

autoplot() draws an overview of every threshold on one intensity axis, or a single method in detail. test_report() writes a report of the test as one web page (and PDF) for the athlete or the coach; report_start() builds one step by step. lactate_report() formats the results as a table for papers. theme_lactater() gives your own plots the same look.

autoplot(<lactate_thresholds>) plot(<lactate_thresholds>)
Plot lactate thresholds
test_report()
A report of a step test, as a web page
report_start() report_header() report_summary() report_zones() report_progress() report_reference() report_prediction() report_checks() report_test() report_methods() report_text() report_page_break() report_save()
Build a test report step by step
lactate_report()
Lactate threshold report table
gt_lactater()
The look of lactater's tables
plot_methods()
Combine lactate threshold methods into one plot
theme_lactater()
lactater ggplot2 theme

Check the analysis

A threshold is only as good as the test behind it. lactate_checks() flags what is easy to miss in a table of numbers, lactate_fit_quality() shows how well each curve follows and predicts the measured lactate, and lactate_diagnostics() plots the regression checks and how much each threshold rests on single stages.

lactate_checks()
Check a lactate threshold analysis
lactate_fit_quality()
Goodness of fit of the lactate curves
lactate_diagnostics() autoplot(<lactate_diagnostics>)
Check the lactate curve and how much each threshold depends on single stages

Use the results

Turn two thresholds of your choice into training zones and count the training time in them; compare two tests of one athlete (is the change real, how far did the curve move, did it shift or change shape), follow a series of tests, measure the test-retest noise of your own protocol, compare athletes per kg or % of peak or with the population of their age and sex, and predict race performance, from published equations or one you calibrate on your own athletes.

lactate_zones() autoplot(<lactate_zones>)
Training zones from two lactate thresholds
training_load() autoplot(<lactate_load>)
Training load and intensity distribution from the lactate zones
compare_tests() autoplot(<lactate_comparison>)
Compare two lactate tests
lactate_reliability()
Test-retest reliability of each threshold, from your own repeated tests
curve_shift()
Shift of the whole lactate curve between two tests
curve_shape() autoplot(<lactate_shape>)
Did the lactate curve shift, or change its shape?
predict_performance() autoplot(<lactate_performance>)
Predict performance from a step test
calibrate_performance() autoplot(<lactate_calibration>)
Calibrate your own performance equation
lactate_trend() autoplot(<lactate_trend>)
Thresholds over a series of tests
relative_thresholds()
Thresholds relative to body mass, peak intensity and peak heart rate
reference_percentiles()
Thresholds against the population

Beyond the step test

The maximal lactate steady state from constant-load bouts, to check which threshold estimates it in your athletes, and the maximal lactate accumulation rate from a sprint test.

lactate_mlss() autoplot(<lactate_mlss>)
Maximal lactate steady state from constant-load bouts
vlamax()
Maximal lactate accumulation rate (VLamax)

Record a test

A web form that records a test and downloads it for lactater, with a printable sheet and a CSV template, to record every test the same way.

recording_sheet()
A sheet to record a step test
read_recording()
Read a recorded step test
